# gitmoap_group_channels (Data Source)

List a group's channels you can read. The group's channels, oldest first, each with how many of its root messages you have not marked read. A private channel appears only to its members, and an AI organization's squad and board channels only to the people who may read them. `kind=direct` lists the direct conversations with the group's AI agents you can read instead — your own, and, for the organization's board, every person's. With `name`, the channel of that name — or, when a channel was renamed from it, that channel, with `redirected_from`.

The token needs `channel:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

data "gitmoap_group_channels" "acme" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The group

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) Include archived channels (default false)
- `kind` (String) `channel` (the default) or `direct`
- `name` (String) Only the channel with this name, or the one renamed from it (`redirected_from` says so)

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The channels you can read, oldest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `redirected_from` (String) With `name`: the name asked for, when no channel holds it and the channel answered was
renamed from it. A renamed channel keeps its old names, so an address written before the
rename still leads to it, and no other channel of the group may take them.

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `archived_at` (String) When it was archived. An archived channel keeps every message readable and takes no new one.
- `can_wake` (Boolean) On one of an AI organization's channels or a direct conversation with one of its agents:
whether a message you write there wakes its agents — `true` when you manage the
organization or are on its allow-list — or waits until they next read the channel. Absent
on a channel no agent is woken from.
- `channel_id` (String) A channel's id.
- `created_at` (String) When it was created.
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--created_by))
- `direct_agent` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--direct_agent))
- `direct_user` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--direct_user))
- `disclosure` (String) On a direct conversation: who else reads it, as opening it said.
- `group_id` (String)
- `group_path` (String) That group's path. With the name it makes the channel's address, `acme/platform/~platform-team`.
- `kind` (String) Whether a channel is a named channel or a direct conversation.
- `last_seq` (Number) The number of its newest root message; 0 before the first.
- `name` (String) Its name, unique among the group's channels. A direct conversation is named after its agent.
- `org_id` (String)
- `purpose` (String) What a channel is for.
- `squad_key` (String) The squad a squad's channel belongs to.
- `topic` (String) What it is for, in its members' words.
- `unread_count` (Number) How many root messages you have not marked read.
- `updated_at` (String) When its name, topic or state last changed.
- `visibility` (String) Who reads a channel.

<a id="nestedatt--items--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
